myth.plants: Indoor plants clean the air — Myth
myth.fresheners: Air fresheners improve air quality — Myth
myth.cloth_mask_fact: Only N95/FFP2 respirators with a proper seal significantly reduce fine particle inhalation. Cloth and surgical masks block large droplets but let most PM2.5 through.
myth.plants_fact: Peer-reviewed studies show that the number of plants needed to measurably reduce PM2.5 in a room is impractically large. A single HEPA purifier outperforms hundreds of plants.
myth.ionizer_fact: Ionizers and ozone generators can produce ozone, a lung irritant, and are far less effective at particle removal than HEPA filters. Some consumer models exceed safe ozone levels.
myth.fresheners_fact: Air fresheners mask odours but add volatile organic compounds (VOCs) and secondary particulate matter to indoor air, worsening overall air quality.

about.title: About AirCompass
about.intro: AirCompass is a GenAI-powered urban air quality assistant. A deterministic physics and exposure engine computes all numbers, while Gemini selects, orders, and explains actions using token references so the model never invents a figure.
about.bullet1: Single-zone indoor mass-balance model with three parameter sets for uncertainty ranges.
about.bullet2: Breathing-weighted 24-hour exposure across sleep, home, commute, and exercise slots.
about.bullet3: US EPA 2024 AQI breakpoints and CPCB India NAQI (PM-based approximation).
about.bullet4: Privacy-first: household profiles stay in your browser's localStorage.
about.privacy: No accounts. No server-side profile storage. No third-party analytics.
